To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gauge invariant quarks canonical momenta are not conserved and the gauge invariant quarts canonical momenta are conserved, and the nucleon momentum decompositions based on them are different and both are consistent with the data.~
the gauge invariant quarks canonical momentum can be defined and that it can be used to construct two theoretically possible decomposition of nucleon momentum into quark and gluon momenta.

the gauge invariant quarks and gluon canonical momentum decomposition of nucleon momentum, which is the only theoretically consistent decomposition, predicts 6% or (if the gluon color field is included in the gluon momentum) 21% of the nucleon’s momentum is carried by the gluons, which is consistent with experimental data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a decomposition of a nucleon’s momentum into quark and gluon components.
the momentum decomposition of the nucleon in QCD and the spin structure of the nucleon.
a fundamental issue in the theory of elementary particles: the decomposition of nucleon momentum into the contributions of quarks and of gluons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proton spin crisis is solved.~
the nucleon momentum is 79% carried by quarks, and either 6% (the most probable) or 21% (the least probable) carried by gluons.
the nucleon spin is not a simple sum of quark and gluon spins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gauge invariant quarks are the only physical degrees of freedom of the QCD vacuum and that the gluons in nucleons do not carry any momentum.
the proton spin crisis is solved by the quark canonical momentum decomposition of the nucleon momentum, and that the proton spin is not carried by gluons.
the gauge invariant quarks and gluon canonical momentum decompositions are both possible and the quark canonical momentum decomposition is the correct one.~
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now predict the momentum carried by gluons in the nucleon.

the gluon momentum fraction in nucleon is not uniquely defined, and the existing experimental results on the gluon momentum fractions in nucleons do not necessarily contradict the proton spin crisis result.
the proton spin crisis is not a crisis at all.
